sec: PSC radiology, histology, treatment; PBC vs PSC comparison table

items.q: Which radiological investigation is marked the investigation of choice (IOC) for PSC?
items.exp: 'MRCP (IOC)' with ERCP listed beneath; both point to 'Strictures/Ectasia'. (Book p1022)

items.q: Fill up: Both MRCP and ERCP in PSC demonstrate ______ / ______ of the bile ducts (image caption).
items.exp: '→ Strictures/Ectasia' and the cholangiogram caption 'Strictures/Ectasia'. (Book p1022)

items.q: What histological feature is printed for PSC (and labelled in the micrograph)?
opts: Florid duct lesion with non-caseating granuloma
items.exp: 'Histological Features : Concentric periductal onion skin fibrosis.' Micrograph caption: 'Concentric periductal fibrosis'. (Book p1022)

items.q: Treatment of PSC on this page is surgery — what recurrence figure is printed?
PBC vs PSC table, row 'Population incidence' — match — 1) PBC 2) PSC … A) Young male B) Perimenopausal females
items.exp: Population incidence: PBC = Perimenopausal females; PSC = Young male. (Book p1022)

items.q: Rows 'Disease type' and 'HLA association' — match — 1) PBC 2) PSC … A) Autoimmune disease; HLA association absent B) Fibrosing disease; HLA association present
items.exp: Disease type: PBC autoimmune, PSC fibrosing. HLA association: PBC absent, PSC present (B-8, DR-3). (Book p1022)

items.q: Row 'Smoking' — judge: I Smoking increases the risk of PBC. II Smoking is protective in PSC.
items.exp: Smoking: PBC = Increase risk; PSC = Protective. (Book p1022)

items.q: Rows 'Disease association' and 'Diagnostic feature' — match — 1) PBC 2) PSC … A) Sjogren's syndrome; AMA Ab B) Ulcerative colitis; MRCP
items.exp: Disease association: PBC Sjogren's, PSC UC. Diagnostic feature: PBC AMA Ab, PSC MRCP (printed 'IOP' in the table, 'IOC' on the same page above). (Book p1022)

items.q: A young man with ulcerative colitis has raised ALP; MRCP shows multifocal strictures and ectasia. Per the comparison table, what is the treatment listed for his condition?
items.exp: The picture is PSC. Table row 'Treatment': PBC = UDCA; PSC = Transplant. (Book p1022)

items.q: Row 'Carcinoma association' — judge: I PBC is not premalignant. II PSC is associated with cholangiocarcinoma.
items.exp: Carcinoma association: PBC = Not premalignant; PSC = A/w cholangiocarcinoma. (Book p1022)

items.q: Which of the following row pairings from the PBC vs PSC table is WRONGLY stated?
opts: Smoking: PBC protective, PSC increases risk
Population: PBC perimenopausal females, PSC young male
Diagnostic feature: PBC AMA Ab, PSC MRCP
items.exp: The smoking row is reversed in this option: the book prints PBC = increase risk, PSC = protective. The other three pairings are correct. (Book p1022)
